paragraphs:
Rav Shmuel bar Shilat; see his entry. He was a teacher of children, a descendant of Haman: Helek. For thirteen years he did not see his garden, so as not to leave his pupils. Rav found him standing in his garden and said, “Have you abandoned your trust?” He answered, “My thoughts are there”: Bava Batra 8b. In Af al Pi: the royal official did not pass by his doorway. Rav Yehudah reports in the name of R' Shmuel bar Shilat, who said in Rav's name: Eruvin 28a; Sukkah 46, end of side b. Rav said to R' Shmuel bar Shila, “Make my eulogy fervent”: Shabbat 153a. Rav Yehudah was his son. In Kahana's name: Jerusalem Megillah, chapter 1, halakhah 11. Rav Mari was the son of Shmuel bar Shilat's daughter.

In Sefer Gilgulei Neshamot: Shamgar ben Anat, who struck six hundred men with an ox-goad, is Rav Shmuel bar Shilat, who taught children, and he stirs his spear. Rav Shmuel was careful to perform his work properly, as in Bava Batra 21a: Rav told Rav Shmuel bar Shilat, “Do not accept a child before six; from then onward, feed him like an ox.” This is “the ox-goad,” melammed ha-bakar: melammed in the sense of a teacher, for he taught them and struck the pupils so that they would learn. Those six hundred men allude to the six orders of the Mishnah, for each order comprises a hundred. End of quotation. For until Hillel they used to teach six hundred orders of Mishnah. In Sefer ha-Kavvanot, Shoftim, in the selections: he was from the root of Kayin, like Sisera. Therefore the initials of “the stars fought from their courses” spell Haman, for both were from one source. End of quotation. This is what the sages explained in Bava Batra 8: “Those who make the many righteous, like the stars forever and ever”—these are teachers of children. Such as whom? Such as Rav Shmuel bar Shilat. The expression “like the stars” concerning Rav Shmuel bar Shilat is directed toward the foregoing secret of Sisera, against whom the stars fought: he is Haman, from whom Rav Shmuel bar Shilat, the teacher of children, descended.
